_about: Quotes copied verbatim from commentary.db chunks (see `source`). Global normalization: whitespace collapsed, ligatures fi/fl expanded, the scanner's quote marks U+2015/U+2016 shown as curly quotes. Per-quote PDF artifact fixes are listed in `extraction_fixes`. voice='commentator' marks Fr. Tadros Malaty's own words (he is not a church father). An ellipsis joins two excerpts from the same chunk; a leading/trailing ellipsis marks an excerpt cut mid-sentence. Rebuild with: python scripts/build_quotes.py

quotes.work: Commentary on Genesis, ch. 3 ("God's care for man")
quotes.quote: God did not wait for man to come to Him to apologize for his sins, but He approached him, so that, by love He would draw him to recognize his sins and to confess them.
quotes.source: ~/projects/commentary.db | chunks.id=174180 | Fr. Tadros Malaty Bible Commentary / 001_Genesis - Fr. Tadros Yacoub Malaty.pdf | PDF p. 60

quotes.work: On the Incarnation, §6
quotes.quote: Surely it would have been better never to have been created at all than, having been created, to be neglected and perish; … It was impossible, therefore, that God should leave man to be carried off by corruption, because it would be unfitting and unworthy of Himself.

quotes.work: Commentary on Exodus, Introduction ("The book of the Passover")
quotes.quote: He came down to His people, as a Cloud to shade them by day, as a symbol of protection; as a pillar of fire, to give them light, as the secret of their enlightenment and as their Leader; As a Rock to quench their thirst; and in the tabernacle to dwell among them.

quotes.work: Commentary on Exodus, Introduction ("The book of freedom")
quotes.quote: God delivered them through Moses from the bondage of Pharaoh. But, even after their crossover, they remained in the bondage of lust by: (1) sitting near the pots of meat in Egypt (Ex. 16: 3), and by (2) their temporary enjoyment of carnal lusts that led them to worship the Egyptian golden calf, that had remained deep in their hearts (Ex. 32).
quotes.source: ~/projects/commentary.db | chunks.id=174706 | Fr. Tadros Malaty Bible Commentary / 002_Exodus - Fr. Tadros Yacoub Malaty.pdf | PDF p. 9

quotes.quote: It was not possible for the Lord to dwell where man persists on doing evil; … It was imperative for God to depart from His old temple that persisted on denial, to set in us a new temple, made by His Holy Spirit.

quotes.quote: God did not visit his creatures only once, but since the beginning of the world, as soon as anyone has turned through the law of promise to the Creator of all, God embraces him in his benevolence, grace and Spirit.

quotes.quote: God gave them coats of skin not silk, a symbol of the toils of repentance. Perhaps the skin may have come from the sacrifice of a lamb so that God might teach Adam and Eve sacrifice, symbolic of Christ's sacrifice on the cross.

quotes.work: Fifty Spiritual Homilies, Homily 47, §14 (trans. A. J. Mason, 1921)
quotes.quote: Glory to Him who has delivered the soul from the bondage of Pharaoh, and has made her His own throne, and house, and temple, and His pure bride …
quotes.source: ~/projects/commentary.db | chunks.id=72537 | Monastic / Fifty Homilies Of St Macarius.pdf | PDF p. 353
quotes.note: MACARIUS FLAG: the database's source is A. J. Mason's 1921 translation, titled 'Fifty Spiritual Homilies of St. Macarius the Egyptian' (i.e. Macarius the Great); Mason's introduction defends that attribution. Modern scholarship assigns these homilies to an anonymous Syrian author, 'Pseudo-Macarius', and the Ancient Christian Commentary volumes in the same database cite them that way. Coptic tradition holds them as St. Macarius the Great's.

quotes.work: On the Incarnation, §9
quotes.quote: You know how it is when some great king enters a large city and dwells in one of its houses; because of his dwelling in that single house, the whole city is honored, and enemies and robbers cease to molest it. … Even so is it with the King of all; He has come into our country and dwelt in one body amidst the many …
quotes.source: ~/projects/commentary.db | chunks.id=7935 | Athanasius of Alexandria / On the Incarnation - Saint Athanasius.pdf | PDF p. 16
